summary.headline: Lenskart Q1 FY27 revenue grew 34% YoY and PAT rose 182% to ₹228 crore, with India same-store sales growth at 18.3%.
summary.overview: Lenskart reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 34% YoY and PAT up 182% to ₹228 crore, versus about ₹530 crore PAT for the whole of FY26. Consolidated product margin crossed 70% for the first time, at about 69% in prior quarters. India revenue grew 30.7% to ₹1,531 crore with pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin at 15.4%, while International revenue grew 38% to ₹1,203 crore with pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin at 10.6%. Management framed the story as a long-term market build (6,100+ unserved pin codes, 78 crore people needing vision correction) and added 455 net new stores in nine months. Figures discussed are proforma, which for Q1 FY27 equal reported numbers.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,531 crore (+30.7%), pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹236 crore at 15.4% margin. Same-store sales growth 18.3%, same pin code sales growth 24%, eye tests 63 lakh (+42.7%), eyewear units 82 lakh (+22.8%); 116 net new stores and 50 new cities added.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,203 crore (+38%, about 29% constant currency), pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin 10.6% vs 4.5%. Eyewear units +37.6%, transacting customers +27.8%, only 16 net new stores; sunglasses units +58.4% on seasonal Q1 peak.

guidance_outlook: International store additions to accelerate in some markets (Thailand, Middle East) in coming years, 'maybe not in this year', pending tech integration.
Management expects continued YoY improvement in international EBITDA margin; did not give a FY27 full-year margin number versus Q1.
Long-term white space: over 6,100 pin codes without a Lenskart store; densification allows at least 3,000 more stores; India points past 10,000 stores.
B by Lenskart: sign-ups above 80,000; a few hundred glasses shipping daily; self-eye test in pilot stores.
Hyderabad plant expected to increase in-house frame manufacturing and reduce currency pressure on product margin over time.
capex_capacity: Q1 store capex ₹75 crore and plant capex ₹132 crore, largely for the Hyderabad facility.
Net 116 India stores and 455 net new stores across the group in nine months, the fastest expansion in company history.
Remote optometry live in 786 stores (up from 168 at FY25 end).
Density in 1,517 existing pin codes rose from 1.5 to 1.6 stores (about 150 net new stores in nine months).
International: Middle East being doubled down on; Thailand adding many stores; Japan economics now supportive of acceleration.
demand_pricing: India SSSG 18.3% (vs 16% a year ago), SPSG 24.3%; management says growth implies market share gains.
Eye tests up 20.5% in International and 42.7% in India; management credits eye tests as top-of-funnel volume driver.
Launched ₹500 eyeglass offering (Hustlr Club) with lenses and warranty; management says unit economics work and cannibalisation is managed via house-of-brands and face-scan app.

Premium: ₹10,000+ share of India price points rose from about 18% (DRHP) to 20%; Owndays prescription sales about ₹1,500 crore; Rodenstock and Tokai progressives at ₹30,000+ about ₹250 crore annually.
Quality now cited by about 60% of single-vision buyers as the top reason to buy from Lenskart, versus price earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion toward 10,000 stores strain same-store sales, and how should currency concerns be viewed given strong gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush said density is adding demand, penetration is about 35%, and older-cohort SSSG is still strong; supply (eye tests per store, wait times) is the constraint. Abhishek said about a large share of revenue is non-INR, providing a natural hedge, and product margin was protected by in-house frames, vendor volume discounts and mix; short-term currency headwinds remain possible.

qa_highlights.question: Is supply, rather than demand, the binding constraint on faster store additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush said Tier 2 requires logistics, manpower and training; remote optometry was the big unlock (700+ stores), and AI eye test and an air-plus-train-plus-bus logistics network are next. Focus is on keeping Tier 1 service standards in smaller towns.

qa_highlights.question: Why was NPS softer, and has it recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush attributed the moderation to confusion over social-media communication on policies, since clarified; he said NPS is bouncing back to near its original level. He cited SSSG accelerating from 16% to 18% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Among product, real estate and talent, which is the biggest constraint over the medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush said talent, particularly engineering talent able to use data and AI to remove bottlenecks, and maintaining agility as the company scales.

qa_highlights.question: How do the International geographies rank on margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek declined to rank; said Thailand and Middle East are in growth phases with early-India-like economics, while mature markets like Singapore and Japan have better economics. Peyush said the unit economics playbook is the same as India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international store and SSG outlook, and what is the Japan plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush said International stores moved from about 100 to 450+ in pace terms, Japan is now economically ready for acceleration, and SSG headroom remains large given D2C shift in Japan.

qa_highlights.question: How is accuracy of remote eye tests tracked, and how is ₹500 down-trading controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush said accuracy is not formally defined; the company monitors process adherence via Tango Eye CCTV scoring and tracks exchanges for power change. For ₹500 cannibalisation, it uses face-scan app journeys and a house-of-brands approach.

qa_highlights.question: What does a ₹500 price point do to profitability at scale, and how do branded lens manufacturing arrangements work?
qa_highlights.answer: Peyush said lower price points are more margin-accretive in absolute terms per unit at scale is not the concern; ASP can fluctuate quarter to quarter. For branded lenses, Lenskart is both manufacturing and brand-licensing partner, starting in India and expanding to international markets.

risks_watch: Same-store sales durability as density rises (1.5 to 1.6 stores per pin code) and NPS recovery after the social-media policy issue.
Currency pressure on product margin; International product margin 77.1% and India 64.2% depend on FX and Hyderabad plant ramp-up.
Conversion of first-time eye-test customers may dip as top-of-funnel grows; wait times and queues need management.
Seasonality: Q1 international margin lifted by sunglasses; Q1 is not a clean run-rate for full-year International margin.
Cannibalisation risk from the ₹500 price point and ASP volatility quarter to quarter.
Talent and engineering capacity to support the expansion pace.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term market-build thesis and unit economics, with reassuring answers on NPS and SSSG. Evasive on specifics: declined to rank International geographies by margin, gave no FY27 full-year international margin number, and did not quantify the ₹500 product drag or accuracy of remote eye tests.
key_quotes: Demand is being added, not divided.
India has not bought its glasses yet.
Penetration is half the India opportunity; the other half is value.
I believe the question mark is gone. What remains is scale.
We set out to sell glasses. What we are building is the infrastructure of vision for the billion people no one has ever served.

adds.what: Hyderabad plant (in-house frame manufacturing); Q1 plant capex ₹132 crore largely for it
Net new stores: 455 across group in nine months (116 India net new in Q1 per segment commentary)

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance given; Q1 revenue +34% YoY with India SSSG 18.3% and 116 net India stores, backed by ongoing store and Hyderabad plant build, but International store adds deferred and no full-year number.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Pre-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin rose to 15.4% in India (from 13.3%) and 10.6% in International (from 4.5%), with management expecting continued YoY International margin improvement, though Q1 is seasonally lifted by sunglasses and currency pressure is a headwind.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Store capex of ₹75 crore and plant capex of ₹132 crore (largely Hyderabad facility) are already under way, with 455 net new group stores added in nine months and 116 net India stores in Q1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India same-store sales growth at 18.3% and eye tests up 42.7% in India, with 116 net new India stores, support continued volume growth; International eyewear units rose 37.6%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Hyderabad plant and store build is already funded, and management frames a long runway (6,100+ unserved pin codes, at least 3,000 more stores via densification), so further store and plant capex announcements are likely to follow.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric FY27 revenue or margin guidance was given; Q1 revenue grew 34% and PAT 182%, but management did not quantify a full-year number and Q1 is a seasonal peak for International.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include currency pressure on product margin (India product margin 64.2%), SSSG durability as density rises from 1.5 to 1.6 stores per pin code, and softer NPS that management says is recovering.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Hustlr Club ₹500 eyeglass offering already launched, B by Lenskart shipping a few hundred glasses daily, and branded lens manufacturing and licensing to expand from India to international markets.

rows.label: International store acceleration (Thailand, Middle East, Japan)
rows.why: Management said store additions will accelerate in Thailand and Middle East in coming years but 'maybe not in this year' pending tech integration, while Japan economics are now supportive; International added only 16 net new stores in Q1.

rows.label: Remote optometry and AI eye test rollout
rows.why: Remote optometry is live in 786 stores (up from 168 at FY25 end), and AI eye test plus logistics network are the next supply unlocks named by management.

rows.label: Premium mix shift
rows.why: Share of ₹10,000+ India price points rose from about 18% to 20%, and Rodenstock and Tokai progressives at ₹30,000+ contribute about ₹250 crore annually, though the ₹500 offering dilutes ASP.

tone.note: Management was confident on store density, SSSG at 18.3%, unit economics and NPS recovery, but evasive on International margin ranking, FY27 full-year margin, the ₹500 product drag and remote eye test accuracy, which analysts pressed on.
